chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made it a condition upon himself to walk to the House of Allah (the Sacred), and every slave of his would be free if he went out with his aunt to Mecca, and he would not hire a mount for her nor accompany her. He said: 'It is not invalid; he should hire a mount for her and she should go out with him.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: It is not invalid / It is not nothing (i.e., it is valid)
key_terms.نَذْر: Vow or pledge to perform an act of worship or good deed

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a man makes a conditional vow to walk to Mecca contingent on his slaves accompanying his aunt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fulfillment of a conditional vow (*nadhr*) where emancipation is tied to a specific act of service. The Imam instructs the vow-maker to hire transport for his aunt and accompany her, thereby satisfying the condition and triggering the slaves' freedom, highlighting the Shia juristic principle that the vow's condition must be actively performed rather than merely observed. This ruling underscores the importance of practical execution in vow fulfillment, ensuring the stipulated event occurs to validate the emancipation.
